title: Hilbert's 17th: The Sharp SOS Threshold of the Motzkin Family
description: For the one-parameter Motzkin family Mₐ(x,y) = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − c·x²y², the sibling entry hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-05 proves the sharp positive-semidefinite (PSD) threshold: Mₐ is non-negative on ℝ² ⟺ c ≤ 3. This entry establishes the complementary sharp sum-of-squares (SOS) threshold: Mₐ is a sum of squares of polynomials ⟺ c ≤ 0. The (⟸) direction is the explicit decomposition Mₐ = (x²y)² + (xy²)² + (√(−c)·xy)² + 1²; the (⟹) direction is a Newton-polytope / coefficient obstruction (the engine of the sibling hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-02), since the x²y² coefficient of Mₐ is the negative number −c whenever c > 0, while in any representation Mₐ = ∑ qᵢ² the degree bound and the vanishing of every pure-power coefficient force [x²y²]Mₐ = ∑ ([xy]qᵢ)² ≥ 0. Combining the two thresholds localizes the PSD ⊋ SOS gap along this family to exactly the half-open interval (0, 3]: the members that are PSD but not SOS are precisely those with 0 < c ≤ 3. So the famous Motzkin point c = 3 is not an isolated witness — the whole interval (0,3] separates the cones, and the SOS cone closes off already at c = 0. The non-SOS direction is packaged as a reusable abstract obstruction not_sos_of_neg_diag. Everything is 0-axiom.

mathlibDependencies.description: The degree-d homogeneous part of a multivariate polynomial. Used (via the sibling oq-02 lemma topsq) to prove the degree bound: the degree-2D component of a sum of squares is the sum of the squares of the top forms, which over ℝ vanishes only if every top form does.
Coefficient of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal of exponent vectors. Drives the pure-axis and x²y² coefficient extractions reused from the sibling entry oq-02.
For 0 ≤ r, (√r)² = r. Supplies the real square root √(−c) (valid since c ≤ 0) used to write the deficit term −c·x²y² = (√(−c)·xy)² as a genuine square in the SOS direction.

originalContributions: A fully elementary, 0-axiom proof of the SHARP SOS threshold for the Motzkin family Mₐ(x,y) = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − c·x²y²: it is a sum of squares of polynomials if and only if c ≤ 0 (theorem motzkinPoly_sos_iff). This is the SOS analogue of the sibling oq-05's sharp PSD threshold (c ≤ 3).

Localizes the PSD ⊋ SOS gap along the family to EXACTLY the half-open interval (0, 3] (theorem motzkinPoly_psd_not_sos_iff): a member is PSD but not SOS iff 0 < c ≤ 3. This shows the classical Motzkin point c = 3 is not an isolated witness — the entire interval separates the PSD and SOS cones, while the SOS cone already closes at c = 0.

Packages the non-SOS direction as a reusable abstract Newton-polytope obstruction not_sos_of_neg_diag: any bivariate real polynomial of total degree ≤ 6 whose six pure-power coefficients (x⁶, x⁴, x², y⁶, y⁴, y²) vanish and whose x²y² coefficient is negative cannot be a sum of squares. The Motzkin family is one instantiation.

Reuses the sibling oq-02 coefficient machinery (degree bound, pure-axis vanishing, x²y² extraction) and the sibling oq-05 family object motzkinPoly and PSD predicate IsPSDMv, demonstrating the modular composition of the Hilbert-17 cluster into a single sharp two-sided result.
prerequisites: Hilbert's 17th problem: positive-semidefinite (PSD) polynomials versus sums of squares (SOS), and the PSD/SOS gap for n ≥ 2 variables.
The Motzkin polynomial as the canonical PSD-but-not-polynomial-SOS example, and its non-SOS proof by coefficient comparison (sibling oq-02).
Newton polytopes of sums of squares: the support of every summand lies in half the Newton polytope of the target.
Real square roots and the fact that a sum of real squares is non-negative.

relatedProblems.relationship: Direct complement: oq-05 proves the sharp PSD threshold (PSD ⟺ c ≤ 3) for the same family; this entry proves the sharp SOS threshold (SOS ⟺ c ≤ 0). Combined, they pin the PSD/SOS gap of the family to exactly (0,3]. This entry imports oq-05's motzkinPoly and IsPSDMv directly.

Engine: oq-02 proves the Motzkin polynomial (c = 3) is not a sum of squares by the coefficient obstruction. This entry imports oq-02's reusable lemmas (degree bound, pure-axis extractions, x²y² coefficient identity) and generalizes the argument to the whole family via not_sos_of_neg_diag.

Sibling (rational SOS side): an explicit rational-function SOS certificate for the Motzkin polynomial. Together with this entry it frames the boundary member c = 3 as PSD, not polynomial-SOS, but SOS of rational functions.

Grandparent: states Artin's theorem and frames the open questions on the computational complexity of deciding SOS membership and on quantifying the PSD/SOS gap. This entry quantifies the gap interval for the canonical family by an exact SOS threshold.

mainTheorems.name: motzkinPoly_sos_iff
mainTheorems.description: Sharp SOS threshold: the Motzkin family member Mₐ(x,y) = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − c·x²y² is a sum of squares of polynomials if and only if c ≤ 0. The SOS cone closes off at c = 0, in contrast to the PSD cone which closes at c = 3 (sibling oq-05).

mainTheorems.name: motzkinPoly_psd_not_sos_iff
mainTheorems.description: The PSD ⊋ SOS gap along the Motzkin family is exactly the half-open interval (0,3]: a member is positive-semidefinite but not a sum of squares iff 0 < c ≤ 3. The Motzkin point c = 3 is therefore not an isolated witness.

mainTheorems.name: not_sos_of_neg_diag
mainTheorems.description: Abstract Newton-polytope obstruction: any bivariate real polynomial of total degree ≤ 6 whose pure-power coefficients x⁶, x⁴, x², y⁶, y⁴, y² all vanish and whose x²y² coefficient is negative is not a sum of squares of polynomials.
mainTheorems.leanType: P.totalDegree ≤ 6 → (coeff (mon 6 0) P = 0) → … → coeff (mon 2 2) P < 0 → ¬ IsSOS P

mainTheorems.name: motzkinPoly_sos
mainTheorems.description: SOS direction: for c ≤ 0 the family member is the explicit sum of squares Mₐ = (x²y)² + (xy²)² + (√(−c)·xy)² + 1², using that the deficit −c·x²y² is itself a square.

mainTheorems.name: motzkinPoly_not_sos
mainTheorems.description: Non-SOS direction: for c > 0 the family member is not a sum of squares, since its x²y² coefficient −c is negative — an instance of the abstract obstruction not_sos_of_neg_diag.

mainTheorems.name: motzkin_three_psd_not_sos
mainTheorems.description: The classical Motzkin polynomial (c = 3) lies in the gap: it is PSD but not a sum of squares of polynomials.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 17th problem asks whether every polynomial non-negative on ℝⁿ is a sum of squares — of polynomials, or at least of rational functions. For n ≥ 2 the polynomial answer is no: Motzkin (1967) gave M(x,y) = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − 3x²y², non-negative everywhere by AM–GM yet not a sum of squares of polynomials. A natural quantitative question is how 'thick' the gap between the PSD and SOS cones is. Embedding the Motzkin polynomial in the one-parameter family Mₐ = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − c·x²y² makes the question concrete: the sibling entry oq-05 shows Mₐ is PSD exactly for c ≤ 3, and this entry shows it is SOS exactly for c ≤ 0. The gap is therefore the whole half-open interval (0,3], not a single point.
overview.keyInsight: Newton-polytope reasoning makes the SOS threshold transparent. The support of Mₐ has vertices (4,2), (2,4), (0,0); half the Newton polytope is spanned by the monomials x²y, xy², 1, whose pairwise products never produce x²y². Hence in any SOS representation the x²y² coefficient is forced to equal ∑ ([xy]qᵢ)² ≥ 0. Since [x²y²]Mₐ = −c, membership in the SOS cone requires −c ≥ 0, i.e. c ≤ 0 — and that bound is achieved by the explicit decomposition (x²y)² + (xy²)² + (√(−c)·xy)² + 1². The same Newton-polytope argument that excludes the Motzkin polynomial excludes every c > 0.
overview.approach: The non-SOS direction is proved once and abstractly as not_sos_of_neg_diag, reusing the degree bound, pure-axis vanishing, and x²y² coefficient identity established in the sibling entry oq-02; the Motzkin family is then a single instantiation. The SOS direction is an explicit square decomposition with √(−c). The family object motzkinPoly and PSD predicate IsPSDMv are imported verbatim from oq-05, so the gap-localization theorem is a direct conjunction of the two thresholds.

conclusion.summary: A 275-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization establishing the sharp SOS threshold of the Motzkin family: x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − c·x²y² is a sum of squares of polynomials if and only if c ≤ 0. Combined with the sibling sharp PSD threshold (c ≤ 3), it localizes the PSD ⊋ SOS gap of the family to exactly the half-open interval (0,3].
conclusion.implications: By exhibiting the gap as a full interval rather than the single Motzkin point, the entry quantifies the PSD/SOS separation for the canonical example and isolates the precise constant (c = 0) at which the SOS cone closes. The reusable obstruction not_sos_of_neg_diag abstracts the Newton-polytope argument for future non-SOS results.
conclusion.futureWork: Extend the abstract obstruction beyond the single x²y² diagonal monomial (e.g. to other affine forms whose Newton polytope has an interior lattice point off the half-polytope), and quantify the SOS/PSD gap for the homogeneous Robinson form, whose non-SOS-ness does not reduce to a single negative coefficient.

sections.title: A Reusable Non-SOS Obstruction
sections.summary: Generalizes the sibling oq-02 degree bound to an arbitrary target P of total degree ≤ 6 (degree_bound'), then proves not_sos_of_neg_diag: a bivariate polynomial of total degree ≤ 6 with vanishing pure-power coefficients (x⁶, x⁴, x², y⁶, y⁴, y²) and a negative x²y² coefficient is not a sum of squares. The proof reuses oq-02's pure-axis extractions and the x²y² coefficient identity, concluding that [x²y²]P = ∑ ([xy]qᵢ)² ≥ 0 contradicts negativity.

sections.title: Coefficients and Degree of the Motzkin Family
sections.summary: Writes the imported family object motzkinPoly c = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ + 1 − c·x²y² in monomial form (motzkinPoly_eq), reads off its coefficients (the six pure powers vanish; [x²y²] = −c), and bounds its total degree by 6 — exactly the hypotheses of the abstract obstruction.

sections.title: The Sharp SOS Threshold
sections.summary: Non-SOS for c > 0 (motzkinPoly_not_sos) by instantiating the obstruction; SOS for c ≤ 0 (motzkinPoly_sos) via the explicit decomposition (x²y)² + (xy²)² + (√(−c)·xy)² + 1²; the two combine into the sharp threshold motzkinPoly_sos_iff: SOS ⟺ c ≤ 0.

sections.title: Localizing the PSD ⊋ SOS Gap
sections.summary: Conjoins the sharp SOS threshold with oq-05's sharp PSD threshold to prove motzkinPoly_psd_not_sos_iff: a family member is PSD but not SOS iff 0 < c ≤ 3. The classical Motzkin polynomial (c = 3) is recorded as a member of this gap (motzkin_three_psd_not_sos).
